{"type":"ReadFile","FileContent":{"content":"1→# D3 — Фаза за фазой: детализация по коду → исполнение; review в конце каждой фазы реализации (2026-10-01, accepted)

Верхний слой оставляет P0–P8 скелетами. Каждая фаза детализируется (`task:plan-design <ID> Pn`)
после закрытия предыдущей, по реальному коду, и сразу исполняется. Design finish и plan-wide
design audit не требуются (`Design Audit: not-required`). Каждая фаза реализации P1–P7 получает
последний read-only пункт `Review Pn` (frontier/high; deliverable — verdict в `findings/`); P4
получает дополнительно срез-review после пайплайна и источников. Найденное review исправляется
в owning item этой фазы до закрытия фазы. Item Review по умолчанию `none`.

10→## Rationale
Девять фаз с ~65 пунктами нельзя честно детализировать заранее: контракты P4–P8 зависят от
фактических сигнатур P1–P3. Владелец выбрал инкрементальный режим и подчеркнул качество;
независимый review в конце фазы дешевле, чем review каждого item, и ловит межпунктовые швы.


# D16 — Группировка исполнения P4 и маршруты исполнителя/reviewer (2026-10-04, accepted)

1. **Уточнение D15 §1 только для исполнения.** Разделение контрактов P4.16–P4.23, владельцы,
   приёмка и порядок D15 сохраняются. Вместо всеобщего `solo` разрешены рекомендованные батчи:
20→
   | Batch | Порядок | Общий контекст |
   |---|---|---|
   | B4a | P4.2 → P4.3 | Каталог, роли, политики, 8 общих Required Reads |
   | B4e | P4.10 → P4.11 | Explain/Gate, ScenarioGenerator, паритет, 8 общих Required Reads |

   Routing каждого участника начинается с `recommended:`. Один пункт закрывается со всеми
   собственными Validation/Deliverables до начала следующего; общий GREEN на батч их не заменяет.
   Остальные Routing rows остаются `solo` с конкретным основанием отдельного допуска.

30→2. **Три последовательности переиспользования контекста.** P4.17 → P4.5 (9 общих Required Reads),
   P4.19 → P4.7 (8), P4.16 → P4.18 (8) рекомендуются для продолжения в той же root-сессии.
   Они не являются Routing-батчами: текущий compiler сортирует номера и требует сплошной числовой
   диапазон. Прежнее предложение пяти Routing-батчей с этими парами не проходит preflight.
   Каждый пункт этих последовательностей имеет свою строку запуска и отдельный `prepare`;
   потребитель начинается после GREEN производителя и своего успешного допуска.
   Продолжение в одном root допустимо только внутри явно авторизованного scope, например
   фазового `task:plan-run <PLAN-ID> P4`; отдельный запуск первого пункта не разрешает второй.
   При нехватке контекста штатный continuity reducer сохраняет checkpoint и выбирает переход.

40→3. **Маршруты.** Рекомендуемый исполнитель реализации — `gpt-6.1-sol/high`; semantic minima
   существующих Routing rows сохраняются. Reviewer — `grok/grok-4.7/high` в независимой read-only
   сессии. Выбор фиксируется в Phase Context, roadmap и handoff; `Routing.Review=none` сохраняется
   как исходный minimum, а переданный `--reviewer grok/grok-4.7 --review-effort high` требует
   автоматического независимого ревью каждого implementation item перед закрытием.
   Все execution-sheet строки задают базовые membership/route; reviewer selector добавляется
   к выбранной команде при запуске и передаётся в `prepare` каждого её implementation item.
   P4.13 и P4.14 остаются отдельными read-only review-пунктами: verdict составляет именно Grok,
   исполнитель не сертифицирует собственную реализацию и не запускает ревью reviewer-отчёта.

50→4. **Границы.** P4.13 — после P4.15, перед P4.8; P4.14 — после P4.23. Тяжёлые DB/boundary/cache/
   transaction/batch/predicate/visibility реализации и CRM/engine qualifications не объединяются.
   СУБД, Redis, replica, type coverage, arch/API и остальные проверки каждого пункта сохранены.
   P4.1 уже GREEN и не переисполняется. Эта правка авторизует планирование, а не выполнение P4.

## Rationale
Батчи экономят повторное чтение и подготовку без объединения item-контрактов. Для непоследовательных
номеров переиспользуется root-контекст, но не обходится существующий batch gate. В оставшейся P4
20 канонических execution-sheet строк вместо 22; при достаточном контексте три solo-последовательности
дают ещё три места для переиспользования одной сессии. Это счёт команд/границ, не измерение стоимости.
60→Количество owner-requested item reviews и обязательных проверок от группировки не уменьшается.


# D18 — Состав и порядок P5, швы, имена и пробелы досье по модели и изменениям (2026-10-07, accepted)

1. **Состав и порядок исполнения.** Номера досье P5.1–P5.5 сохраняются. Новые пункты (D3: следующий свободный номер):
   **P5.6** — Review P5 (read-only, последний), **P5.7** — запись динамических прав (create/update/delete),
   **P5.8** — каталоги поиска (directories) по умолчанию и `LookupContext` фазы Assignment. Порядок исполнения
   следует зависимостям кода, не номерам: **P5.2 → P5.7 → P5.4 → P5.8 → P5.5 → P5.3 → P5.1 → P5.6**. Все пункты
   solo (как D16 для тяжёлых P4): каждый — отдельный bounded запуск со своими проверками.
70→   Причины: трейт и `SubjectAccess` (P5.1) — публичная поверхность над пайплайном (P5.2/P5.7), событиями (P5.4),
   менеджерами (P5.3) и движком P4, поэтому идут последними; `RoleCatalog::all(): list<RoleSchema>` и
   `PermissionManager::all(): list<PermissionSchema>` (P5.3) требуют значений схемы P5.5; directories P5.8
   используют Assignment-eligibility P5.2, а схема P5.5 называет классы directories по умолчанию из P5.8.

2. **Владение событиями.** Досье называет «события после commit» в P5.2 и P5.4. P5.2 создаёт `ChangeEffect`
   (kind, type, before/after, `eventId`) и `ChangeResult::$correlationId`, но не диспетчеризует событий; вся доставка
   (каталог 08 §6, after-commit publisher, журнал audit, P11, V34/V35) — P5.4. Причина: без каталога событий P5.2
   пришлось бы вводить временный транспорт; внутреннее Laravel-событие-посредник отвергнуто — `Event::fake()` хоста
   глушило бы публичные события.
80→
3. **Регрессии P13/P11/P14.** Владельцы не меняются (P13 — P5.2, P11 — P5.4, P14 — P1.2). P5.2 и P5.4 закрывают
   spec на уровне `ChangePipeline` (Status `covered:`); сценарий spec на `$user->guard('admin')` добавляет P5.1 в те же
   файлы `tests/Regression/P13Test.php`, `P11Test.php`, `P14Test.php` (сквозной V22).

4. **Имена и места (досье 04 §3 внутренне противоречит зонам 04 §2 — принят слой зон).**
   - `AzGuard\Changes\{Change, ChangeType, ChangeContext, ChangeResult, ChangeStatus, ChangeEffect, EffectKind,
     GrantRecord, GrantDetails}` — `@api` значения P5.2; `PermissionRecord`, `PermissionDetails` — P5.7;
     `GrantFilter`, `GrantPage` — P5.3. `ChangePipeline`, `ActingActor`, `ChangeJournal` (P5.4) — внутренние/`@api`
     по пункту. **`GrantRecord` переносится из P5.3 в P5.2** (уточнение D6): его возвращает `ChangeResult`.
90→   - Arch: `Contracts\Sources\StoresGrants` и `Sources\Database` получают узкое исключение — используют только
     перечисленные value-классы `Changes\*` (не `ChangePipeline`, не менеджеры). Без него `StoresGrants::apply(Change):
     ChangeResult` (D8) нарушает правила «Contracts не импортирует реализации» и «Sources ↛ Changes»; 04 §2 разрешает
     Contracts «публичные immutable definitions … Change inputs».
   - `SubjectAccess`, `SubjectPanels` — `AzGuard\Concerns\` рядом с `HasAzGuard`, а не `Authorization\` (04 §3):
     они пишут через Changes, а правило «Authorization ↛ Changes» блокирующее.
   - Интерфейсы `Contracts\Changes\{GrantManager, PermissionManager}`, `Contracts\Roles\RoleCatalog`, `Contracts\AzGuardSubject`
     (04 §3); реализации `Changes\{ScopedGrantManager, ScopedPermissionManager}`, `Catalog\CodeRoleCatalog`.
     Внутренняя фабрика `Changes\PanelManagers` выдаёт их до `PanelAccess` (P6.1).
   - Схема — `Schema\{PanelSchema, PermissionSchema, RoleSchema, FieldSchema, AssignmentScopeBindingSchema,
100→     AssignmentScopeTypeSchema, TenantTypeSchema, SubjectTypeSchema}` (публичны по расположению), построитель
     `Schema\SchemaBuilder` (внутренний). `SourceDescription` получает `label` и `fields` (D8).
   - События — `Events\{AccessEvent, EventType, PermissionCreated, PermissionUpdated, PermissionDeleted, RoleGranted,
     RoleRevoked, RoleGrantUpdated, PermissionGranted, PermissionRevoked, PermissionGrantUpdated, GrantExpired,
     PanelStateTouched, AccessDecided}`; плагин — `Plugins\Audit\{AuditPlugin, RecordChange}`; таблица
     `{prefix}audit_log` создаёт `StorageSchema` (версия схемы хранилища остаётся 1: 1.0 не выпущен, D01).

5. **Исключения изменений.** P5.2 вводит `UnknownRoleException` (`unknown_role`), `RoleNotGrantableException`,
   `PanelNotWritableException`, `AssignmentScopeNotAcceptedException` (`context_not_accepted`),
   `AssignmentScopeRequiredException` (`context_required`), `TenantRequiredException`, `TenantMismatchException`,
110→   `ChangeCancelledException`, `StaleSelectionException` (UpdateGrant с fingerprint пишет P5.2; P5.3 открывает его через `GrantManager`). **Пробел досье:** класс отказа exact-выдачи
   PolicyOnly-права (R63, 20 F09) не назван — вводится `PermissionNotGrantableException` (`permission_not_grantable`,
   `ChangeException`). **Не вводятся:** `RoleNotEditableException` (в 1.0 нет API изменения definitions, D13/D80) и
   `ResourceScopeMissingException` (в P5 нет точки выброса; в проверке это причина отказа P4). Все — дети
   `ChangeException`, код = 05 §10. `PanelMismatchException` из 05 §1 не вводится: тот же случай (явный `guard:` другой
   панели у `SubjectAccess`) — существующий `ConflictingPanelException` (03 глоссарий, 09 §1).

6. **Пробелы досье заполнены так.**
   - Актор: явный стек → пользователь auth guard панели → `ActorRef::system('console')` в консоли → `null`;
     `ChangeContext::$actor` — `?ActorRef` (18 §10 пишет `ActorRef`, но D23 разрешает изменение без актора; NULL
120→     честнее фиктивного system).
   - `Field::model` на tenant-панели проверяется через `Panel::resourceScopes()` модели (08 §3, D12): нет резолвера —
     `InvalidChangeFieldsException`, а не пропуск.
   - `until <= now` при выдаче — `InvalidChangeFieldsException` с ключом `until` (I7).
   - Listener exception после commit — `report()` и доставка остальных событий; mutation не откатывается и не
     повторяется (08 §6, D49).
   - Prune истёкших (операция) — P5.4, команда `azguard:grants:prune` — P6.6; FormerKeys-миграция (операция и
     dry-run) — P5.3, команда `azguard:roles:rename-key` — P6.6; удержание журнала audit задаётся
     `AuditPlugin::make(retentionDays:)`, очистка — P6.6, doctor `AuditTableExists` — P6.4.
   - Ручной `touch` с `PanelStateTouched` — внутренняя операция `ChangePipeline::touch()` в P5.4; публичный
130→     `PanelAccess::touch()` — P6.1.
   - `permissionSet(on:)`/`permissionNames()` — назначенные Grants-права квалифицированных вкладов выбранного scope
     (роли развёрнуты по PHP-каталогу, прямые выдачи, `GrantedToAll`; суперадмин — все Grants-ключи каталога tenant);
     PolicyOnly не входит; `validUntil` — минимальный срок. Это не окончательное решение (16 §8): `decide()` остаётся
     источником истины.

7. **Остаток вне P5.** `PanelAccess`, фасад `panel()/actingAs()/check()/authorize()` — P6.1; middleware и queue
   context — P6.2/P6.10; команды rename-key/prune/audit — P6.6; doctor — P6.4; UI/editor/autocomplete — P7;
   установленный внешний consumer и матрица Laravel 11/12/13 для `guard()` — P8.4/P8.7. Полная карта —
   `@plan/knowledge/P5-change-model.json` раздел «Карта приёмки».
140→
## Rationale
Досье разносит одно сквозное изменение по пяти пунктам, но код P5.1 и P5.3 вызывает код P5.2/P5.4/P5.5;
порядок по номерам заставил бы вводить временные типы, что запрещено (D14 п.3). Новые P5.7/P5.8 выделяют
отдельные контракты (dynamic actions, directories), чтобы каждый запуск помещался в одну сессию исполнителя
уровня implementation. Узкие arch-исключения и перенос SubjectAccess сохраняют блокирующие правила зон 04 §2,
вместо того чтобы ослаблять их ради расхождения в 04 §3. Заполненные пробелы выбраны fail-closed и названы,
чтобы исполнитель не импровизировал (план: «расхождение досье → D#»).


150→# D20 — Исправление дизайна P5: mutation-контракты, runtime, историческая миграция и приёмка (2026-10-07, accepted)

1. Исправленный P5-change-model (Protocol/Validation/Writes/Composite/Delivery/Build-host-fence) и owning item-контракты — нормативное уточнение D18. Exactly-one next/terminal и тот же writer-owned result; skip/double/fabricated return отменяют всю mutation. Write-side locked reads не подменяются публичным DatabaseSource readSession/memo в host tx.
2. Typed Change.scope=AccessScope; nullable subject/role для action/touch, immutable selection expectedFingerprint/grantId, PermissionDetails для dynamic metadata. Матрица применимости F проверок по типам: action не требует grant subject/eligibility, delete сохраняет dynamic capability/tenant checks. Только until/fields обычной операции mutable; F1 защищает identity/metadata.
3. Проверять и нормализовать expiry/fields ДО F6; trusted proposed — только schema-validated. Scopes AssignmentScopeRuntime получает additive proposed и nullable actor, LookupContext actor nullable; Assignment target обязателен. Change context после with/retry свежий; общий guarded predicate engine один в Scopes для Access/Assignment/Directories, запреты зон и Access regression сохраняются.
4. StateResult/audit/event — frozen resulting revision своего активного Storage-root, capture locked incarnation/version+effect/generation/fingerprint; нет postcommit reread/escaped handle. Nested Storage-root children — один bump; два отдельных pipeline-вызова внутри host tx — два bumps и snapshots v+1/v+2. Публикация ждёт внешний host commit; historical token события не latest freshness guarantee. Tentative result не cache.
5. Dynamic delete — planned per-row RevokePermission exact stored grants выбранного tenant со всеми stored origins, затем action-only DeletePermission. Cancel любой revocation откатывает всё. Pattern grants и другой tenant не затронуты; removed ids aggregate, effects authoritative.
6. FormerKeys — INTERNAL MigrateRoleGrant из locked stored rows/registered destination/from∈formerKeys и отдельной actor delegation через pipes, НЕ Revoke+ordinary Grant. Private capability нельзя взять из fields/request, ordinary grant/update не имеет bypass. Сохраняются historical id/tenant/context/subject/origin/expiry/fields (expired/orphan/inactive/old schema); live F2/F5/F6/F7/F8 здесь не применяются, но Access eligibility и no widening остаются обязательными. Pipe может отменить, не изменить historical payload. Collision — existing to-row, max expiry (NULL∞), to-fields, source delete; dry-run без writes/events/audit. Текущие active определения всё равно могут отказывать historical grants; old→new передаётся before/after audit/RoleGrantUpdated.
7. TouchPanel — typed panel-wide global-scope planned Change (Inspection, immutable reason/no grant record), always effective touch/effect, changing/audit/event path с previousVersion/eventId. AccessDecided — отдельный read tracing: ordinary decision dispatch сразу, recognized joint tx deferred; no tracing=zero dispatch и нет PolicyOnly Storage prerequisites.
8. P5.2 сохраняет immutable compiled subjects(model,guard,directory); P5.5/P5.8 consume descriptor, не восстанавливают потерянный рецепт. Directory describe проверяет type/ref/tenant даже Inspection; arbitrary owner callback не выдумывается SQL column. Predicate SQL + stable candidate chunks/tenantOf до accepted limit, не postfilter final page. Assignment scope search без selected subject=[]; targetless выбор SubjectDirectory не создаёт fake runtime. Custom directories/auth guard не теряются.
160→9. P5.3 cleanup учитывает exact permissions удалённые/Grants→Policy, keyset cursor bound к server partition/filter/build. R42 real revoke одной origin сохраняет независимые relation/manual/external witnesses. P5.4 принимает R27 actor reason/audit отказа. V102/V110 чужие смыслы убраны из карты, конкретные V109/V111/V112/V113 P5 slices названы; P5.6 получает Pint/types/diff и required execution findings.
10. R29 package fence: snapshot Registry build/panel под state lock, stale expected form/build refusal; strict concurrent host deployment/owner change требует collaborating host marker/row/revision locks на том же PDO. Fixture pipe и barrier tests — P5.2, cleanup P5.3; реальный consumer deploy/host transfer — P8.7. Универсальная таблица/сервис active build не вводится; один cached registry hash не доказывает distributed safety.
11. Owning P5.4 включает DatabaseSource writer TouchPanel и его task_files: active mutation → touch → Applied record=null/records=[]/Updated effect. Internal MigrateRoleGrant.phase=Inspection; maintenance/Revocation/touch ChangeContext.proposed=[] вместо выдачи historical raw fields за schema-validated input. Поля доступны только как protected stored payload. Expired/inactive/missing host subject/context сохраняют соответствующий Access отказ; old-schema unknown keys сами по себе не deny — текущие conditions решают. Explicit FormerKeys rename может восстановить authority текущей роли при сохранении partition/expiry. P5.6 V9 требует D20 negative controls и итоговый verdict после V1–8/V10–12.

## Rationale
Устранить реальные несовместимости между per-row pipes, final validation, исторической миграцией, runtime frames, mutation lifecycle и приёмочными владельцами. Исполнитель не должен угадывать исключения к security/transaction/schema правилам. Уточнения сохраняют принятые зоны, code-role definitions, partition и owner gates; новые обходы обычной выдачи не разрешаются.


# D23 — Размещение публикатора событий и внутренние методы writer в P5.4 (2026-10-07, accepted)

170→1. Внутренний публикатор — `Changes\ChangeEventPublisher` (не `@api`, вне манифеста); `Events\` содержит только значения: `AccessEvent`, `EventType`, 12 событий. Имя и роль из D18 п.4 сохраняются, меняется только пространство имён.
2. `Sources\Database` в P5.4 расширяется внутренними методами writer: `DatabaseSource::{afterCommit, afterAuthorityCommit, appendJournal, tenantsWithExpired}` и `LockedReads::expired`, помимо writer-пути TouchPanel. Новых публичных значений они не вводят; прямой записи вне ChangePipeline по-прежнему нет.
3. Файлы, которые пункт затрагивает неизбежно: `AzGuardServiceProvider` (scoped-привязка `ChangeJournal`), `tests/Fixtures/Storage/{DdlSnapshot,SchemaAssertions,ddl/*.json}` (таблица audit_log в снимках DDL), `tests/Unit/Changes/ChangeValuesTest.php` (новый case enum), `tests/Fixtures/Events/**`.

## Rationale
Не раздувает публичный API ради расположения класса и не вводит обходной доступ к хранилищу из Changes; альтернатива — исключение в генераторе манифеста — меняет гейт совместимости вне пункта.

фактических сигнатур P1–P3. Владелец выбрал инкрементальный режим и подчеркнул качество;
независимый review в конце фазы дешевле, чем review каждого item, и ловит межпунктовые швы.


# D16 — Группировка исполнения P4 и маршруты исполнителя/reviewer (2026-10-04, accepted)

1. **Уточнение D15 §1 только для исполнения.** Разделение контрактов P4.16–P4.23, владельцы,
   приёмка и порядок D15 сохраняются. Вместо всеобщего `solo` разрешены рекомендованные батчи:

   | Batch | Порядок | Общий контекст |
   |---|---|---|
   | B4a | P4.2 → P4.3 | Каталог, роли, политики, 8 общих Required Reads |
   | B4e | P4.10 → P4.11 | Explain/Gate, ScenarioGenerator, паритет, 8 общих Required Reads |

   Routing каждого участника начинается с `recommended:`. Один пункт закрывается со всеми
   собственными Validation/Deliverables до начала следующего; общий GREEN на батч их не заменяет.
   Остальные Routing rows остаются `solo` с конкретным основанием отдельного допуска.

2. **Три последовательности переиспользования контекста.** P4.17 → P4.5 (9 общих Required Reads),
   P4.19 → P4.7 (8), P4.16 → P4.18 (8) рекомендуются для продолжения в той же root-сессии.
   Они не являются Routing-батчами: текущий compiler сортирует номера и требует сплошной числовой
   диапазон. Прежнее предложение пяти Routing-батчей с этими парами не проходит preflight.
   Каждый пункт этих последовательностей имеет свою строку запуска и отдельный `prepare`;
   потребитель начинается после GREEN производителя и своего успешного допуска.
   Продолжение в одном root допустимо только внутри явно авторизованного scope, например
   фазового `task:plan-run <PLAN-ID> P4`; отдельный запуск первого пункта не разрешает второй.
   При нехватке контекста штатный continuity reducer сохраняет checkpoint и выбирает переход.

3. **Маршруты.** Рекомендуемый исполнитель реализации — `gpt-6.1-sol/high`; semantic minima
   существующих Routing rows сохраняются. Reviewer — `grok/grok-4.7/high` в независимой read-only
   сессии. Выбор фиксируется в Phase Context, roadmap и handoff; `Routing.Review=none` сохраняется
   как исходный minimum, а переданный `--reviewer grok/grok-4.7 --review-effort high` требует
   автоматического независимого ревью каждого implementation item перед закрытием.
   Все execution-sheet строки задают базовые membership/route; reviewer selector добавляется
   к выбранной команде при запуске и передаётся в `prepare` каждого её implementation item.
   P4.13 и P4.14 остаются отдельными read-only review-пунктами: verdict составляет именно Grok,
   исполнитель не сертифицирует собственную реализацию и не запускает ревью reviewer-отчёта.

4. **Границы.** P4.13 — после P4.15, перед P4.8; P4.14 — после P4.23. Тяжёлые DB/boundary/cache/
   transaction/batch/predicate/visibility реализации и CRM/engine qualifications не объединяются.
   СУБД, Redis, replica, type coverage, arch/API и остальные проверки каждого пункта сохранены.
   P4.1 уже GREEN и не переисполняется. Эта правка авторизует планирование, а не выполнение P4.

## Rationale
Батчи экономят повторное чтение и подготовку без объединения item-контрактов. Для непоследовательных
номеров переиспользуется root-контекст, но не обходится существующий batch gate. В оставшейся P4
20 канонических execution-sheet строк вместо 22; при достаточном контексте три solo-последовательности
дают ещё три места для переиспользования одной сессии. Это счёт команд/границ, не измерение стоимости.
Количество owner-requested item reviews и обязательных проверок от группировки не уменьшается.


# D18 — Состав и порядок P5, швы, имена и пробелы досье по модели и изменениям (2026-10-07, accepted)

1. **Состав и порядок исполнения.** Номера досье P5.1–P5.5 сохраняются. Новые пункты (D3: следующий свободный номер):
   **P5.6** — Review P5 (read-only, последний), **P5.7** — запись динамических прав (create/update/delete),
   **P5.8** — каталоги поиска (directories) по умолчанию и `LookupContext` фазы Assignment. Порядок исполнения
   следует зависимостям кода, не номерам: **P5.2 → P5.7 → P5.4 → P5.8 → P5.5 → P5.3 → P5.1 → P5.6**. Все пункты
   solo (как D16 для тяжёлых P4): каждый — отдельный bounded запуск со своими проверками.
   Причины: трейт и `SubjectAccess` (P5.1) — публичная поверхность над пайплайном (P5.2/P5.7), событиями (P5.4),
   менеджерами (P5.3) и движком P4, поэтому идут последними; `RoleCatalog::all(): list<RoleSchema>` и
   `PermissionManager::all(): list<PermissionSchema>` (P5.3) требуют значений схемы P5.5; directories P5.8
   используют Assignment-eligibility P5.2, а схема P5.5 называет классы directories по умолчанию из P5.8.

2. **Владение событиями.** Досье называет «события после commit» в P5.2 и P5.4. P5.2 создаёт `ChangeEffect`
   (kind, type, before/after, `eventId`) и `ChangeResult::$correlationId`, но не диспетчеризует событий; вся доставка
   (каталог 08 §6, after-commit publisher, журнал audit, P11, V34/V35) — P5.4. Причина: без каталога событий P5.2
   пришлось бы вводить временный транспорт; внутреннее Laravel-событие-посредник отвергнуто — `Event::fake()` хоста
   глушило бы публичные события.

3. **Регрессии P13/P11/P14.** Владельцы не меняются (P13 — P5.2, P11 — P5.4, P14 — P1.2). P5.2 и P5.4 закрывают
   spec на уровне `ChangePipeline` (Status `covered:`); сценарий spec на `$user->guard('admin')` добавляет P5.1 в те же
   файлы `tests/Regression/P13Test.php`, `P11Test.php`, `P14Test.php` (сквозной V22).

4. **Имена и места (досье 04 §3 внутренне противоречит зонам 04 §2 — принят слой зон).**
   - `AzGuard\Changes\{Change, ChangeType, ChangeContext, ChangeResult, ChangeStatus, ChangeEffect, EffectKind,
     GrantRecord, GrantDetails}` — `@api` значения P5.2; `PermissionRecord`, `PermissionDetails` — P5.7;
     `GrantFilter`, `GrantPage` — P5.3. `ChangePipeline`, `ActingActor`, `ChangeJournal` (P5.4) — внутренние/`@api`
     по пункту. **`GrantRecord` переносится из P5.3 в P5.2** (уточнение D6): его возвращает `ChangeResult`.
   - Arch: `Contracts\Sources\StoresGrants` и `Sources\Database` получают узкое исключение — используют только
     перечисленные value-классы `Changes\*` (не `ChangePipeline`, не менеджеры). Без него `StoresGrants::apply(Change):
     ChangeResult` (D8) нарушает правила «Contracts не импортирует реализации» и «Sources ↛ Changes»; 04 §2 разрешает
     Contracts «публичные immutable definitions … Change inputs».
   - `SubjectAccess`, `SubjectPanels` — `AzGuard\Concerns\` рядом с `HasAzGuard`, а не `Authorization\` (04 §3):
     они пишут через Changes, а правило «Authorization ↛ Changes» блокирующее.
   - Интерфейсы `Contracts\Changes\{GrantManager, PermissionManager}`, `Contracts\Roles\RoleCatalog`, `Contracts\AzGuardSubject`
     (04 §3); реализации `Changes\{ScopedGrantManager, ScopedPermissionManager}`, `Catalog\CodeRoleCatalog`.
     Внутренняя фабрика `Changes\PanelManagers` выдаёт их до `PanelAccess` (P6.1).
   - Схема — `Schema\{PanelSchema, PermissionSchema, RoleSchema, FieldSchema, AssignmentScopeBindingSchema,
     AssignmentScopeTypeSchema, TenantTypeSchema, SubjectTypeSchema}` (публичны по расположению), построитель
     `Schema\SchemaBuilder` (внутренний). `SourceDescription` получает `label` и `fields` (D8).
   - События — `Events\{AccessEvent, EventType, PermissionCreated, PermissionUpdated, PermissionDeleted, RoleGranted,
     RoleRevoked, RoleGrantUpdated, PermissionGranted, PermissionRevoked, PermissionGrantUpdated, GrantExpired,
     PanelStateTouched, AccessDecided}`; плагин — `Plugins\Audit\{AuditPlugin, RecordChange}`; таблица
     `{prefix}audit_log` создаёт `StorageSchema` (версия схемы хранилища остаётся 1: 1.0 не выпущен, D01).

5. **Исключения изменений.** P5.2 вводит `UnknownRoleException` (`unknown_role`), `RoleNotGrantableException`,
   `PanelNotWritableException`, `AssignmentScopeNotAcceptedException` (`context_not_accepted`),
   `AssignmentScopeRequiredException` (`context_required`), `TenantRequiredException`, `TenantMismatchException`,
   `ChangeCancelledException`, `StaleSelectionException` (UpdateGrant с fingerprint пишет P5.2; P5.3 открывает его через `GrantManager`). **Пробел досье:** класс отказа exact-выдачи
   PolicyOnly-права (R63, 20 F09) не назван — вводится `PermissionNotGrantableException` (`permission_not_grantable`,
   `ChangeException`). **Не вводятся:** `RoleNotEditableException` (в 1.0 нет API изменения definitions, D13/D80) и
   `ResourceScopeMissingException` (в P5 нет точки выброса; в проверке это причина отказа P4). Все — дети
   `ChangeException`, код = 05 §10. `PanelMismatchException` из 05 §1 не вводится: тот же случай (явный `guard:` другой
   панели у `SubjectAccess`) — существующий `ConflictingPanelException` (03 глоссарий, 09 §1).

6. **Пробелы досье заполнены так.**
   - Актор: явный стек → пользователь auth guard панели → `ActorRef::system('console')` в консоли → `null`;
     `ChangeContext::$actor` — `?ActorRef` (18 §10 пишет `ActorRef`, но D23 разрешает изменение без актора; NULL
     честнее фиктивного system).
   - `Field::model` на tenant-панели проверяется через `Panel::resourceScopes()` модели (08 §3, D12): нет резолвера —
     `InvalidChangeFieldsException`, а не пропуск.
   - `until <= now` при выдаче — `InvalidChangeFieldsException` с ключом `until` (I7).
   - Listener exception после commit — `report()` и доставка остальных событий; mutation не откатывается и не
     повторяется (08 §6, D49).
   - Prune истёкших (операция) — P5.4, команда `azguard:grants:prune` — P6.6; FormerKeys-миграция (операция и
     dry-run) — P5.3, команда `azguard:roles:rename-key` — P6.6; удержание журнала audit задаётся
     `AuditPlugin::make(retentionDays:)`, очистка — P6.6, doctor `AuditTableExists` — P6.4.
   - Ручной `touch` с `PanelStateTouched` — внутренняя операция `ChangePipeline::touch()` в P5.4; публичный
     `PanelAccess::touch()` — P6.1.
   - `permissionSet(on:)`/`permissionNames()` — назначенные Grants-права квалифицированных вкладов выбранного scope
     (роли развёрнуты по PHP-каталогу, прямые выдачи, `GrantedToAll`; суперадмин — все Grants-ключи каталога tenant);
     PolicyOnly не входит; `validUntil` — минимальный срок. Это не окончательное решение (16 §8): `decide()` остаётся
     источником истины.

7. **Остаток вне P5.** `PanelAccess`, фасад `panel()/actingAs()/check()/authorize()` — P6.1; middleware и queue
   context — P6.2/P6.10; команды rename-key/prune/audit — P6.6; doctor — P6.4; UI/editor/autocomplete — P7;
   установленный внешний consumer и матрица Laravel 11/12/13 для `guard()` — P8.4/P8.7. Полная карта —
   `@plan/knowledge/P5-change-model.json` раздел «Карта приёмки».

## Rationale
Досье разносит одно сквозное изменение по пяти пунктам, но код P5.1 и P5.3 вызывает код P5.2/P5.4/P5.5;
порядок по номерам заставил бы вводить временные типы, что запрещено (D14 п.3). Новые P5.7/P5.8 выделяют
отдельные контракты (dynamic actions, directories), чтобы каждый запуск помещался в одну сессию исполнителя
уровня implementation. Узкие arch-исключения и перенос SubjectAccess сохраняют блокирующие правила зон 04 §2,
вместо того чтобы ослаблять их ради расхождения в 04 §3. Заполненные пробелы выбраны fail-closed и названы,
чтобы исполнитель не импровизировал (план: «расхождение досье → D#»).


# D20 — Исправление дизайна P5: mutation-контракты, runtime, историческая миграция и приёмка (2026-10-07, accepted)

1. Исправленный P5-change-model (Protocol/Validation/Writes/Composite/Delivery/Build-host-fence) и owning item-контракты — нормативное уточнение D18. Exactly-one next/terminal и тот же writer-owned result; skip/double/fabricated return отменяют всю mutation. Write-side locked reads не подменяются публичным DatabaseSource readSession/memo в host tx.
2. Typed Change.scope=AccessScope; nullable subject/role для action/touch, immutable selection expectedFingerprint/grantId, PermissionDetails для dynamic metadata. Матрица применимости F проверок по типам: action не требует grant subject/eligibility, delete сохраняет dynamic capability/tenant checks. Только until/fields обычной операции mutable; F1 защищает identity/metadata.
3. Проверять и нормализовать expiry/fields ДО F6; trusted proposed — только schema-validated. Scopes AssignmentScopeRuntime получает additive proposed и nullable actor, LookupContext actor nullable; Assignment target обязателен. Change context после with/retry свежий; общий guarded predicate engine один в Scopes для Access/Assignment/Directories, запреты зон и Access regression сохраняются.
4. StateResult/audit/event — frozen resulting revision своего активного Storage-root, capture locked incarnation/version+effect/generation/fingerprint; нет postcommit reread/escaped handle. Nested Storage-root children — один bump; два отдельных pipeline-вызова внутри host tx — два bumps и snapshots v+1/v+2. Публикация ждёт внешний host commit; historical token события не latest freshness guarantee. Tentative result не cache.
5. Dynamic delete — planned per-row RevokePermission exact stored grants выбранного tenant со всеми stored origins, затем action-only DeletePermission. Cancel любой revocation откатывает всё. Pattern grants и другой tenant не затронуты; removed ids aggregate, effects authoritative.
6. FormerKeys — INTERNAL MigrateRoleGrant из locked stored rows/registered destination/from∈formerKeys и отдельной actor delegation через pipes, НЕ Revoke+ordinary Grant. Private capability нельзя взять из fields/request, ordinary grant/update не имеет bypass. Сохраняются historical id/tenant/context/subject/origin/expiry/fields (expired/orphan/inactive/old schema); live F2/F5/F6/F7/F8 здесь не применяются, но Access eligibility и no widening остаются обязательными. Pipe может отменить, не изменить historical payload. Collision — existing to-row, max expiry (NULL∞), to-fields, source delete; dry-run без writes/events/audit. Текущие active определения всё равно могут отказывать historical grants; old→new передаётся before/after audit/RoleGrantUpdated.
7. TouchPanel — typed panel-wide global-scope planned Change (Inspection, immutable reason/no grant record), always effective touch/effect, changing/audit/event path с previousVersion/eventId. AccessDecided — отдельный read tracing: ordinary decision dispatch сразу, recognized joint tx deferred; no tracing=zero dispatch и нет PolicyOnly Storage prerequisites.
8. P5.2 сохраняет immutable compiled subjects(model,guard,directory); P5.5/P5.8 consume descriptor, не восстанавливают потерянный рецепт. Directory describe проверяет type/ref/tenant даже Inspection; arbitrary owner callback не выдумывается SQL column. Predicate SQL + stable candidate chunks/tenantOf до accepted limit, не postfilter final page. Assignment scope search без selected subject=[]; targetless выбор SubjectDirectory не создаёт fake runtime. Custom directories/auth guard не теряются.
9. P5.3 cleanup учитывает exact permissions удалённые/Grants→Policy, keyset cursor bound к server partition/filter/build. R42 real revoke одной origin сохраняет независимые relation/manual/external witnesses. P5.4 принимает R27 actor reason/audit отказа. V102/V110 чужие смыслы убраны из карты, конкретные V109/V111/V112/V113 P5 slices названы; P5.6 получает Pint/types/diff и required execution findings.
10. R29 package fence: snapshot Registry build/panel под state lock, stale expected form/build refusal; strict concurrent host deployment/owner change требует collaborating host marker/row/revision locks на том же PDO. Fixture pipe и barrier tests — P5.2, cleanup P5.3; реальный consumer deploy/host transfer — P8.7. Универсальная таблица/сервис active build не вводится; один cached registry hash не доказывает distributed safety.
11. Owning P5.4 включает DatabaseSource writer TouchPanel и его task_files: active mutation → touch → Applied record=null/records=[]/Updated effect. Internal MigrateRoleGrant.phase=Inspection; maintenance/Revocation/touch ChangeContext.proposed=[] вместо выдачи historical raw fields за schema-validated input. Поля доступны только как protected stored payload. Expired/inactive/missing host subject/context сохраняют соответствующий Access отказ; old-schema unknown keys сами по себе не deny — текущие conditions решают. Explicit FormerKeys rename может восстановить authority текущей роли при сохранении partition/expiry. P5.6 V9 требует D20 negative controls и итоговый verdict после V1–8/V10–12.

## Rationale
Устранить реальные несовместимости между per-row pipes, final validation, исторической миграцией, runtime frames, mutation lifecycle и приёмочными владельцами. Исполнитель не должен угадывать исключения к security/transaction/schema правилам. Уточнения сохраняют принятые зоны, code-role definitions, partition и owner gates; новые обходы обычной выдачи не разрешаются.


# D23 — Размещение публикатора событий и внутренние методы writer в P5.4 (2026-10-07, accepted)

1. Внутренний публикатор — `Changes\ChangeEventPublisher` (не `@api`, вне манифеста); `Events\` содержит только значения: `AccessEvent`, `EventType`, 12 событий. Имя и роль из D18 п.4 сохраняются, меняется только пространство имён.
2. `Sources\Database` в P5.4 расширяется внутренними методами writer: `DatabaseSource::{afterCommit, afterAuthorityCommit, appendJournal, tenantsWithExpired}` и `LockedReads::expired`, помимо writer-пути TouchPanel. Новых публичных значений они не вводят; прямой записи вне ChangePipeline по-прежнему нет.
3. Файлы, которые пункт затрагивает неизбежно: `AzGuardServiceProvider` (scoped-привязка `ChangeJournal`), `tests/Fixtures/Storage/{DdlSnapshot,SchemaAssertions,ddl/*.json}` (таблица audit_log в снимках DDL), `tests/Unit/Changes/ChangeValuesTest.php` (новый case enum), `tests/Fixtures/Events/**`.

## Rationale
Не раздувает публичный API ради расположения класса и не вводит обходной доступ к хранилищу из Changes; альтернатива — исключение в генераторе манифеста — меняет гейт совместимости вне пункта.

Audit plugin writes to ChangeJournal during the mutation transaction, but only after the pipeline and terminal apply complete. Journal entries are not written during pipe execution.

AuditPlugin writes occur after the pipeline completes, so a subsequent failure rolls back the journal entry along with the transaction. The contract requires the audit pipe to return the same result and write only after exactly-once next, so the plugin ordering needs verification. Storage::perform registers callbacks via connection->afterCommit at the end of work, before the transaction callback returns; Laravel fires these when the outermost transaction commits.

ChangePipeline registers afterCommit callbacks inside the work callback via writer->afterCommit. Storage::perform then registers those callbacks on the connection at the end of the outermost transaction, even when the mutation is nested. This means nested mutations may trigger afterCommit callbacks prematurely.

Nested Storage::mutate callbacks are registered on the connection immediately when the nested perform returns, not deferred to the parent mutation's callback list. They still wait for the outermost connection commit.

Nested storage mutations use savepoints within the outer connection transaction. If the inner savepoint rolls back but the outer transaction commits, afterCommit callbacks registered during the nested work may still fire.

Need to verify whether Laravel discards afterCommit callbacks from nested transactions that roll back, or if they survive to fire on outer commit. Also need to inspect how `$reads->token($effects)` projects the state token—whether it uses v+1 or rereads.

Need to verify that no-op changes do not trigger unnecessary touch operations. PermissionDeleted must source removedGrantIds from the planned change rather than a later result state. When two pipeline calls run inside one host transaction, Storage::mutate nests and increments version only if parent is null.

The version bump is gated by `$parent === null`, not by the host transaction level. When two pipeline calls run inside a plain database transaction, each is treated as a Storage root and increments the version once. The nested flag only affects retries and authority transactions.

Nested Storage mutations that spawn from a parent mutation should bump version only once. This nesting path needs test coverage.

The `assertBuild` check compares the captured PanelRegistry identity against a fresh container resolve. It catches in-process registry replacement during the lock. Cross-process deployments are handled by the fence pipe.

MariaDB assertion counts are 58 higher than on other databases despite identical test suites. This likely reflects StorageDdlTest enumerating more columns or indexes on MariaDB rather than indicating a bug.

Continuing the thorough review.

A potential bug was identified in GrantWriter::apply. The method caches context based on Change object identity. During pipeline processing, objects may be bound to frames or copied via withUntil/withFields. This could cause finalize() to retrieve the wrong cached context when comparing $planned and $final.

The context caching concern is resolved. A new Change object from withUntil triggers fresh validation. The final object's context remains correct. This is not a bug.

A bug was found in GrantWriter::apply. The method receives a new Change object from `finalized()`. This object is different from the one cached during `finalize()`. The context cache key changes. The validator re-runs and recomputes the context.

The re-validation in GrantWriter::apply is harmless. It should pass.

A new concern was found in Model D20. sameIdentity excludes until and fields. A pipe could call withUntil or withFields on a MigrateRoleGrant without breaking identity. This may violate the immutability requirement.

Migration roles cannot call withUntil or withFields through the API. The sameIdentity check excludes until and fields. A pipe could construct a Change object with identical identity but different until or fields values.

The migration path does not re-check until or fields against the stored row. It only compares role, scope, and fingerprint. A Change with identical identity but different until would pass this check.

GrantWriter::migrate writes only the role column. It ignores change->until entirely. The migration path uses source and target until values from stored rows for collision checks.

The writer correctly ignores mutated until values. It enforces the immutability rule by using stored payload instead of the Change object's fields.

For migrations, proposed fields remain empty because proposes() and proposesFields() are false. The writer relies on the stored row, which is correct.

Touch origin validation occurs before the touch early return in finalize.

Revocation returns before eligibility checks. The writer deletes the stored row without using proposed fields, so this path is safe.

For Create and Update actions, withFields can modify fields. Finalize revalidates them via actionFields, which rejects non-empty fields. This behavior is correct.

Delete action skips context() entirely. It returns after stored() without calling context(). This is safe because Delete cannot use withFields.

sameIdentity compares label, group, and description. It does not compare details->fields. withFields mutates both fields and details.fields via copy(). Grants allow field changes. Actions revalidate them. Migrations reject withFields. This is acceptable.

A potential bug was spotted in Create action. The catalog overlay lookup may run before the prefix check.

The Create action calls catalog overlay before the prefix check. A second catalog lookup may throw PrefixConflictException. The LockedReads::catalog implementation needs inspection.

State token projection via LockedReads::token($effects) must be checked for correct v+1 projection without reread.

Events should not contain models. AccessEvent uses ActorRef, TenantRef, StateToken, and GrantRecord fields. GrantRecord or event toArray must be inspected for model inclusion.

PermissionDeleted pulls removedGrantIds from the frame's prior results. The pipeline records each change before emitting its events. This ordering ensures the DeletePermission event captures only revoked grants.

PermissionRevoked events are built from individual effect records, not from the frame's removedGrantIds, so revoke ordering is safe.

The audit plugin writes journal entries inside the transaction while events dispatch after commit. This separation is correct.

Listener exceptions are caught and reported by dispatch(). A test should verify this behavior.

A potential issue with nested host transactions and the committed flag is being examined.

The nested transaction logic is correct. When a host transaction already exists, the result flags it as nested and leaves committed false. For non-nested operations, the storage transaction commits before run() returns, so marking committed true is accurate.

Laravel dispatches events via afterCommit during the transaction commit phase, before the transaction callback returns to the caller. ChangeResult is therefore returned with committed=true, and the result object already contains the dispatched events.

The ChangeResult is created after the transaction returns, so it already contains the dispatched events. Those events use state captured inside the transaction via `$reads->token($effects)`, avoiding a reread.

A potential issue was noted with the `afterCommit` closure capturing `$events` and `$this->events`. If event objects are mutable, a listener could alter their public properties, which would change the payload for subsequent listeners.

The Model requirement that a later mutation listener must not alter an already-captured event payload is satisfied if events are value objects with readonly properties.

GrantWriter only increments the version when effects are non-empty. A no-op run produces no effects, so the version stays unchanged. Multiple changes in one run still trigger a single storage increment because pending touches are deduplicated into a set.

The token projection for no-op children inside a root with effective siblings is being verified. The operation result uses the final token derived from the total effect count, so it correctly reflects v+1 when effects exist. Individual change results may retain their own tokens.

The token projection logic is being verified. `touch()` returns a state token at `token(1)` before the outer version increment occurs, so `token()` must project `v+1` without reading the database row. A second pipeline call inside one host transaction is also under review.

Two separate pipeline calls inside one host transaction each have a null parent, so both increment the version. If a second call runs inside the first's transaction callback, the parent exists and only one version bump occurs.

Laravel's `afterCommit` inside a nested transaction fires only when the outermost commit completes. Storage::mutate wraps its work in a savepoint via `connection->transaction`, so the committed flag and event dispatching are deferred until the host transaction fully commits.

A potential bug was spotted in Storage::perform. It registers afterCommit callbacks for mutation callbacks unconditionally, even when the transaction is nested. This could cause premature event dispatching.

Tests should verify that afterCommit callbacks registered inside nested transactions are deferred until the outer commit.

Journal entries written during the pipe are rolled back on transaction rollback, which is correct.

The AuditPlugin must be checked to ensure it writes through ChangeJournal without importing Storage directly.

The Authorizer tracing path needs inspection to confirm AccessDecided exceptions do not trigger events before root commit.

ScopedGrantManager and GrantInspection predicates still need review for IDOR coverage.

The review scope expanded to include QueryScopeDirectory limits, SchemaBuilder secrets, HasAzGuard trait guards, CRM README honesty, and vacuous acceptance tests. To handle the volume, subagents will be spawned for parallel inspection of specific areas while the highest-risk code is still read directly. The immediate focus is concrete bugs in LockedReads::token version projection, ChangeResult::combine state handling, deletePermission planning, RoleKeyMigration, ScopedGrantManager partitioning, QueryScopeDirectory search/describe logic, and SchemaBuilder serialization.

A potential GrantWriter::migrate collision was examined. When the target version equals the source, the migration deletes the source without updating the target, which is correct because deletion is an effect. If the versions differ, the target is updated and its existing fields are preserved per the model requirement.

When both the target and source versions are identical and no expiry changes, the migration still deletes the source and emits a Deleted effect. The version bumps once because effects remain non-empty.

If the source row is missing, StaleSelectionException is thrown instead of Unchanged. Dry-run behavior is handled separately.

replace() compares only until and fields for no-op equality, ignoring actor differences. Updating identical until and fields yields Unchanged even when the actor differs.

The fingerprint logic must be checked to confirm it includes build. Revocation of foreign partition grants also needs review.

Continuing the deep review.

Checking `LockedReads::token` for version projection bugs. Also found a potential issue in `ChangeResult::combine`: the `inTransaction()` check runs before the writer transaction starts, so a non-transactional caller may incorrectly report committed=true.

The `ChangeResult::combine` concern is unfounded. Laravel commits the transaction before returning, so `afterCommit` callbacks fire during commit. The `committed=true` result is correct for the outer case.

Nested host transactions are handled correctly. When the host already has an open transaction, Storage::mutate detects it and creates a savepoint. Laravel only runs afterCommit callbacks when the outermost transaction commits.

Confirmed that nested storage mutations register `afterCommit` callbacks. Laravel defers their execution until the root transaction commits. If the outer host transaction rolls back, those callbacks are skipped.

Confirmed version bumping: root mutations increment the token once per pipeline call, while nested mutations share the parent and do not double-bump. Touch operations are always effective.

Touch tenant scope is verified. `run()` uses `TenantRef::global()`, and `Change::touchPanel` applies `AccessScope::in(TenantRef::global())`. The identity check in F1 correctly skips F2-F11 for tenant panels.

Checking whether `touch()` returns a StateToken that correctly reflects the projected version versus the individual result state. Need to inspect the `token()` implementation.

Also examining journal write ordering inside pipes. If an audit pipe appends before `$next`, the journal row is written before the writer and rolled back on failure. The model requires exactly-once `next` semantics, so `AuditPlugin` must be verified.

Custom pipes that write before `$next` could emit a journal row for an `Unchanged` change if they do not check effects. The built-in `AuditPlugin` should only write when effects exist.

`events()` iterates over result effects, so `Unchanged` changes correctly produce no events.

A sequencing bug was found: `events()` is called before `frame->record($result)`, yet it reads `$change->removedGrantIds()`, which depends on `frame->removed()`. This means the permission deletion event may capture stale or empty removed grant IDs.

The sequencing concern is resolved. DeletePermission revoke changes record their results before the parent delete change emits events, so removedGrantIds reads prior revokes from frame->removed(). The parent change's own result is not needed for grant IDs.

Revoke pipe failures correctly trigger transaction rollback, preventing the delete change from running.

If the action is missing, DeletePermission is still planned but fails validation with UnknownPermissionException, so the mutation rolls back cleanly. No database writes occur when no grants exist.

When the action exists, grants are revoked before the delete change executes.

Checking that `grantsNamed` filters by exact tenant and name, not patterns.

The `migrate()` method updates the stored row's role but does not rewrite the actor from the change actor on the simple move path. The D20 composite specification says actor delegation passes through changing pipes separately, so the stored actor should remain.

The migration pipe cannot change the payload. `sameIdentity` does not include the `until` field.

Confirmed that `sameIdentity` intentionally excludes `until` and `fields`. Migration changes therefore cannot use `withUntil` or `withFields`, since `proposes()` is false for them. The remaining concern is whether a pipe could construct a new Change with different `until` or `fields` values while still passing identity checks.

The concern about a pipe constructing a new Change with different until or fields while passing identity checks is resolved. GrantWriter::migrate ignores those fields and writes the stored database row directly. The migration payload cannot be altered by the pipe.

Migration `until` values are read from the source and target rows, not the change object. Ordinary grants may legitimately modify fields via `withFields`. A pipe could still construct a Change with altered `until` or `fields` that passes `sameIdentity`, but the writer ignores those fields and writes the stored payload directly. This raises a question about whether F1's maintenance payload contract is violated.

The F1 contract requires maintenance payloads to be immutable. A pipe that constructs a Change with altered until or fields while passing sameIdentity would silently discard those changes rather than throwing InvalidConfigurationException. This is a violation of the immutability requirement.

Silent payload substitution is a contract deviation. The model explicitly requires InvalidConfigurationException on any payload change attempt. The next step is to inspect the Change constructor and its visibility to determine whether pipes can construct altered Change objects.

Checking whether the Change constructor is private. If it is, pipes cannot forge altered until or fields values, closing the F1 payload substitution gap.

Action details fields are properly validated. sameIdentity compares label, group, and description but not details->fields. withFields is allowed for create and update permissions, and finalize's action() calls context()->actionFields to reject non-empty fields, preventing invalid changes.

sameIdentity correctly includes name, touch reason, and expectedFingerprint. This prevents pipes from altering those fields without detection.

Ordinary grants may legitimately change until or fields via withUntil and withFields. The context() validation step runs before eligibility(), matching the required F7/F8-before-F6 ordering.

However, a pipe can invoke $change->context() during its own execution, which triggers validation before finalize completes.

ChangeFrame caches context per Change object. A pipe that calls context() on the planned change stores a cached result. If the pipe returns withUntil(), finalize validates the new object because it is not cached. Change objects are immutable, so pipes cannot mutate state through this path.

Eligibility correctly consumes the validated `context->proposed` value.

For revocation, `proposes()` is false, so the proposed array is empty. Historical raw expiry and fields remain on the Change object but are excluded from the new schema proposal. The model treats these as immutable raw values that do not pass through validation.

Change exposes its fields publicly, so pipes can read historical values directly.

The model explicitly requires historical fields to remain as protected stored payload, not as validated proposed values. If Change exposes its fields publicly, pipes can read raw historical data directly.

Checking whether the Change property should be protected rather than merely excluded from proposed values. The write-side tenant check uses a direct Eloquent query on the host model instead of a DatabaseSource readSession, which risks reading stale or uncommitted data outside the writer transaction.

The host model lookup for field tenant is distinct from the locked reads of grants and catalog. The contract does not explicitly require this lookup to use the writer PDO, so a replica connection could return stale data.

The Eloquent host-model query is not a DatabaseSource readSession, so it may safely use the same connection. A replica could still return stale data, but this seems minor.

Next items to inspect:
- QueryScopeDirectory LIMIT behavior
- ScopedGrantManager for IDOR risks
- SchemaBuilder closures
- CRM README
- Acceptance test vacuity

Subagents will be spawned to parallelize coverage of large areas. They will report candidate findings with file:line references for manual verification. The highest-risk code will still be read directly, including token(), Change properties, AuditPlugin, race tests, and managers.

A read outside the lock was found in pruneExpired: tenantsWithExpired is called before the loop begins, then each batch mutation proceeds separately.

The pre-read tenant list in pruneExpired is acceptable for a batch job. A tenant that gains an expired grant between listing and mutation will be handled on the next run. This is not a blocker.

tenantsWithExpired queries the storage table, not the mutation table, so its read outside the transaction is harmless for discovery.

planRoleKeyMigration holds the lock during a read-only transaction and commits it without writing or touching panel_state, so the version stays unchanged.

assertBuild compares panel instances by object identity rather than by value.

assertBuild correctly catches registry replacement and in-place panel mutation because object identity changes. The remaining risk is whether fingerprint recomputation during build would detect code definition changes that mutate the role catalog without replacing the panel instance. This depends on whether fingerprint is cached at build time.

Stale fingerprint from in-process class mutation is an acknowledged package fence limitation. The contract binds to immutable registry buildId and fingerprint, so compile-time fingerprint is accepted as-is and not treated as a finding if documented.

HostFencePipe and race tests must be inspected to confirm they assert zero writes.

The assertion count difference between V4 (276) and earlier versions (218) for the same 24 tests likely reflects MariaDB schema differences rather than a regression. Extra assertions on MariaDB probably come from reporting more columns or indexes, not from skipped tests.

Continuing the thorough review.

A potential bug was found in `LockedReads::token()`. It increments the state version by the total effects count from the entire pipeline run. This may incorrectly project the token version for individual change results.

The token projection bug is confirmed. No-op changes report state version v, while effective changes report v+1. The specification requires all effective children of one active Storage-root to share a common v+1. This mismatch violates the rule that committed=false does not guarantee a final parent token.

The token projection is actually correct for a single Storage-root. Each effective child adds exactly one to the locked version, so multiple effective changes within one run all share a common v+1.

A nested mutation issue was identified instead. If a mutation is nested inside another Storage mutation that already touched the panel, the locked state version may already be the pre-parent version because the lock is taken once.

The nested mutation theory was abandoned. Separate pipeline calls are independent Storage-roots, so they do not share a locked version. The focus shifted to `Storage::perform` and how the locked state is assigned when `parent === null`.

The nested mutation theory is confirmed. When `Storage::mutate` is called inside an active mutation, the parent is not null, so the version increment is skipped. The child token projects from the outer lock's pre-incremented version instead of the already-incremented one.

The nested mutation theory was abandoned. The child token projection is correct: one bump at the outer root, and no-op states are explicitly permitted.

A new potential bug was found in composite operations. Events are built per individual change result using `$result->state`, which is the per-change token rather than the combined pipeline token.

The composite operation event bug is confirmed. The specification requires a single Storage-root to share one final token across all nested changes. Individual change results project `token(1)` for each effect, while the combined result projects `token($effects)`. This mismatch violates the rule that multiple changes in one run must have a common final token.

The composite operation event bug is resolved. All effective changes in one run share the same projected version v+1, satisfying the common final token requirement. StateToken equality holds for identical components. Touch and delete permission cascades are unaffected.

No-op revokes produce no events, which is correct. Events from separate pipeline calls inside a host transaction carry distinct projected versions; this is acceptable because publication waits for the host commit via `afterCommit`, and `Storage::perform` registers those callbacks on the connection.

Checking Laravel's `afterCommit` semantics inside savepoints. The review is examining whether callbacks registered during a nested `Storage::mutate` call execute at the correct transaction level.

Laravel's `afterCommit` callbacks are only executed when the transaction counter reaches one, meaning they fire at the outermost commit level. Nested savepoints therefore cannot trigger these callbacks prematurely.

Confirmed that nested savepoints correctly defer afterCommit callbacks until the host transaction commits. Need to verify that Laravel's root rollback clears those callbacks.

A critical Laravel gotcha was identified. Callbacks registered during a nested savepoint are appended to the shared `afterCommitCallbacks` array and are not cleared on rollback. They therefore fire at the outer commit even though the savepoint rolled back. This means nested `Storage::mutate` calls risk publishing events for failed changes.

The review is now examining Laravel's `transaction()` source to determine whether afterCommit callbacks registered inside a nested savepoint are discarded when that savepoint rolls back.

The review is now inspecting Laravel's `handleTransactionException` to confirm whether a failed nested savepoint's `rollBack` discards its appended `afterCommit` callbacks. If those callbacks survive rollback, a failed nested mutation could still publish events at the outer commit. Storage's own retry logic for concurrency errors is also being checked.

Checking whether the existing test for nested rollback verifies that no events were published. If the test only checks version and keys, a gap remains where failed nested mutations could still trigger unwanted events at the outer commit.

Confirmed that multiple effects within a single change, such as GrantWriter migrate returning both an update and a delete, still project exactly one version bump. The aggregate token logic in ChangePipeline correctly applies this single increment across all effects. No-op changes remain at the pre-incremented version.

Storage::perform increments only touched panels. Actor changes are excluded from equality checks, which is correct. Revocation finalization skips live existence and grantability checks after early returns for identity and origin label. The tenant scope check runs before revocation, preventing tenant changes during revocation. Origin labels are asserted on revocation sources.

Stored origins are assumed valid because invalid ones would cause prune and revoke failures. Touch operations skip F2 through F11 checks after the origin assertion, which requires IdentityCodec rules to permit 'panel' as a valid origin label. Migration checks catalog former keys and stored fingerprint, scope, and role, but intentionally omits subject existence, eligibility, and expiry validations. The tenant partition check during migration is also being examined.

The `sameIdentity` method intentionally excludes `until` and `fields` from its comparison. Migration operations do not call `proposes()`, so they bypass the `assertProposes` check that would otherwise require a proposal.

Migration payloads are immutable. The `withUntil` method throws, and `withFields` requires a proposal or create/update permission that migrations lack. Because the `Change` constructor is private and its public static factories are internal, pipes cannot construct altered migration changes. Any attempt to change identity would fail `sameIdentity`, so historical payloads remain fixed.

sameIdentity compares name, details label, group, and description, but not details.fields. withFields can change fields, yet actionFields rejects non-empty fields for actions while grants allow them.

The review is now tracing the exact validation order in grant finalization, checking whether F7 and F8 run before F6.

The review traced the exact validation order in grant finalization. F7 and F8 run via `validator->context()` before F6, which is acceptable because pipes may invoke context early to fail fast. A potential cache bug in ChangeFrame was also noted.

The ChangeFrame context cache is safe. A pipe that returns a new object via `withUntil()` triggers fresh validation at the terminal stage. If a pipe passes the original unchanged object, the cached context is reused without issue.

Eligibility checks read from the validated proposed context rather than raw change fields. Revocation and touch operations correctly yield empty proposed arrays. The review is now examining migration context.

Migration context yields an empty proposed array. Historical fields remain public on Change::$fields, so pipes can read them as stored payload. This is acceptable because they are not presented as validated proposal.

The "protected" qualifier refers to schema immutability, not PHP visibility. Historical raw fields remain public on Change::$fields but are intentionally excluded from ChangeContext.proposed, so pipes cannot treat them as validated proposal data.

The review found that revocation safely handles missing actions by adding a DeletePermission change, which the validator rejects with UnknownPermissionException and prevents partial writes. If the action exists, revocation and deletion proceed together and any pipe cancellation rolls back the entire transaction.

Two new concerns emerged: grantsNamed must return only exact grants within the tenant without patterns or cross-tenant matches, and managers need ScopedGrantManager to prevent IDOR. A Directory LIMIT issue was also noted.

QueryScopeDirectory is needed for directory queries. SchemaBuilder needs toArray support. AccessEvent payloads must be checked for Eloquent model inclusion. A test should confirm that listener exceptions do not roll back mutations, since dispatch catches Throwable and delivery occurs after commit. The audit plugin writes journal entries during pipes inside the transaction; rollback removes them.

AuditPlugin must skip unchanged changes. The dispatch location of AccessDecided still needs to be found. A search for grant-table mutations found only StorageSchema, GrantWriter, ActionWriter, and DatabaseSource audit writes; no other direct inserts or updates were discovered.

Storage and plugin writes are being checked for additional mutations. Eloquent saves are guarded. The tenant discovery in pruneExpired reads tenant lists outside the panel lock, but each tenant is processed in its own mutation under lock, so this is safe.

planRoleKeyMigration holds the panel lock but performs only reads. It returns a migration plan without writes, touches, journal entries, or events. The transaction commits cleanly and leaves the version unchanged.

Storage::mutate acquires the panel lock before executing the transaction body. The assertBuild check runs after the lock is already held, and catalog reads occur inside lockedReads within that same locked scope. This ordering is correct.

HostFencePipe executes inside the locked transaction, satisfying the state-lock-to-host-fence-lock model. assertBuild compares registry instance, buildId, fingerprint, and panel identity to detect stale selections. A race test uses a host marker pipe rather than replacing the in-process registry, because separate processes maintain independent registries.

The package check is in-process identity. Cross-process deploy is the fixture pipe. That's what D20 says: package fence + fixture, real consumer deploy is P8.7.

### Potential bug: assertBuild uses `$this->container->make(PanelRegistry::class)` INSIDE the lock and compares to the registry captured BEFORE the lock. If they're the same singleton and buildId matches, OK. A coordinated deploy in another process doesn't change this process's registry. The fixture pipe checks the host marker. Good.

### Grant fingerprint includes build

GrantRows line 72.

Field tenant validation queries host models via their default connection instead of the writer mutation connection. This is a host model lookup, not a grant read, so it does not violate D20's rule against write-side locked reads being replaced by public DatabaseSource reads.

A replica-configured host model could return stale or missing tenant data during field validation. The contract only requires Panel::resourceScopes(), not the writer PDO, so this is a separate issue from D20's write-side locked-read rule.

content.text: The race tests assert real lock order and rollback. I’ll check event publication on a nested rollback, then the managers, directories, and acceptance claims.

content.thinking:
Continuing a deep review to identify actual contract violations.

Checking six high-risk areas: nested rollback in ManagesTransactions, QueryScopeDirectory LIMIT and tenant logic, ScopedGrantManager IDOR, schema serialization, HasAzGuard guard(array), and README status claims for P5.1/P5.3.

R36, R47, R63, and R68 still mark completed P5 items as future work. The review is checking whether these stale claims are false GREENs or merely underclaims.

Stale "future" claims are conservative underclaims, not dangerous dishonesty. The real issue is false GREEN or passing statuses that lack a corresponding test. The review will verify that every claim marked as passing has a real test asserting it.

R07 is a partial status, not a false pass. The review is now spawning subagents to walk acceptance tests in parallel while reading the riskiest code. A potential token projection bug was spotted in LockedReads::token($effects): it adds +1 if effects > 0 based on the locked version at the start.

The LockedReads token projection is correct. Child results and combined results share the same version plus one. No-op children keep state v with committed=false, matching the model's specification.

The review is now inspecting nested host transaction event publication in ManagesTransactions. It must verify whether callbacks registered inside a savepoint leak to the outer commit on rollback, which would be a blocker.

Remaining items to examine include QueryScopeDirectory search logic, GrantInspection predicates and cursor, schema toArray closures and secrets, HasAzGuard guard behavior, FormerKeys bypass, and write-outside-pipeline architectural exceptions.

D18 p.4 lists Change value classes for StoresGrants and Database sources. GrantFilter and GrantPage are P5.3 values, but they are value classes rather than pipeline or manager classes. The expanded list in AZGUARD_CHANGE_VALUES is acceptable.

The review is verifying that Sources do not import ChangePipeline or managers. The test `azguardForbiddenChangeReferences` covers this.

StorageMutation is correctly isolated to Storage, Database, ChangePipeline, and Testing. ChangeJournal uses a closure instead of StorageMutation. ChangeEventPublisher does not use Storage. Plugin imports are being checked.

A potential bug was spotted in DatabaseSource. Its methods tenantsWithExpired and tenantsHolding call `$storage->table()` outside the lock from pruneExpired and RoleKeyMigration. This risks using the wrong connection.

The off-lock tenant scans in DatabaseSource risk races. A tenant could appear or disappear between listing and processing. Missing a tenant until the next prune may be acceptable. RoleKeyMigration likely lists tenants before migrating each one. planRoleKeyMigration holds the lock for the full plan read but does not run pipes.

migrateRoleKey runs pipes per row. This is correct.

Delete permission handling was verified. If action is null, the planned DeletePermission change throws UnknownPermissionException and rolls back the mutation. No orphan is created. If action exists, grants are revoked before deletion.

A pipe that cancels a revoke rolls back the entire mutation before the delete change is applied. The cascade cancel test must be verified to assert rollback of both the action and grants.

The field tenant check uses Eloquent `::query()->find()`. This is a host model read, not a DatabaseSource readSession, so D20 does not apply.

The field tenant lookup is a separate host model read, not a DatabaseSource call. D20 p.3 only restricts locked reads inside the host transaction. If the host model uses a replica connection, it could see stale data or uncommitted writes.

The field tenant check is F8. It does not explicitly require the host model read to run on the writer PDO. The review is weighing whether this omission is a contract violation.

The field tenant lookup is speculative and will not be reported unless tests show a concrete split-connection failure.

Origin labels "panel" and "dynamic" must be verified against IdentityCodec::assertSourceLabel.

Revocation correctly returns before subject and role checks.

A bug was spotted in Migration::sameIdentity: it omits `until` and `fields` from the identity comparison.

F1 forbids changing `until` and `fields` via the public API. Migration pipes cannot use `withUntil` or `withFields`. The constructor is private, so pipes cannot build a new Change with different values directly. The remaining risk is whether a pipe could call `Change::migrate()` with a modified `GrantRecord`.

A pipe could tamper with `until` or `fields` in a migrated grant record. `sameIdentity` would not catch this because it omits those fields from its comparison. The migration check also does not verify that the change's `until` matches the stored row's `until`. This creates a concrete bypass path for altering expiration or field data during migration.

GrantWriter::migrate writes the stored database row, not the change's until or fields. A tampered payload is ignored. This may violate F1, which forbids substituting the stored payload.

The silent ignore of tampered `until` or `fields` during migration is a contract violation. The model requires `InvalidConfigurationException` when a pipe tries to alter payload, but the code silently discards the change instead. Whether a pipe can actually pass a different `until` is uncertain because `Change` is readonly and `withUntil` throws.

The review is now probing whether the tampered-payload bypass is observable. If a pipe can construct a GrantRecord with the same fingerprint but different until, sameIdentity returns true and the writer silently ignores the altered until. The key question is whether this produces any observable effect.

The tampered-payload bypass is a minor finding. The mutation succeeds with the original expiry, so the security property holds and no data is altered. The pipe receives no exception because F1 does not compare until or fields, and the writer re-reads the stored row. D20 permits cancellation but not payload modification.

The silent acceptance of tampered payload during migration is now judged as a major normative contract violation. The observable effect is incorrect error handling rather than data corruption. The review is weighing whether silent acceptance versus throwing InvalidConfigurationException constitutes an observable effect.

PermissionDeleted removedGrantIds is read from the change frame. The journal writes events during the pipe via RecordChange, before the current change is recorded.

The pipeline dispatches events after the pipe completes and after the current change is recorded. The test would fail if the listener exception were not swallowed, because the exception escapes mutate() before it returns. The later permission grant still proves the process continues after the error.

The test does not prove delivery of a second event in the same batch, but it does serve as a negative control against exception propagation. The code loops with try/catch, and the test would fail without it. This is sufficient coverage, so I will not flag this as a major untested gap.
